scheme_name: "Reactivation Of Fisheries Cooperative Societies" Component of the "Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana" Scheme
description:
The "Reactivation of Fisheries Cooperative Societies" is a vital component of the "Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana" scheme launched by the Government of India in 2020. 

This scheme aims to support the livelihoods of fishermen and enhance the fisheries sector in the state of West Bengal. 

The Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana was initiated on 12th November 2020. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to reactivate and strengthen fisheries cooperative societies that have become dormant or inactive. 

The government aims to revitalize these societies to ensure better income and livelihood for fishermen. 

The reactivation process is expected to benefit approximately 1.5 million fishermen across the state. 

The scheme specifically targets societies that have not been functioning effectively for a period of time. 

The government has set a measurable target of reactivating at least 500 cooperative societies within the first year of implementation. 

The benefits under this scheme include financial assistance for infrastructure development, training programs, and capacity building for cooperative members. 

Each cooperative society can receive up to ₹5 lakh for reactivation purposes. 

This financial assistance is aimed at improving the operational capabilities of the societies. 

The scheme also includes provisions for providing modern fishing equipment to enhance productivity. 

Fishermen associated with these societies will receive training on sustainable fishing practices. 

The government aims to ensure that at least 70% of the fishermen trained under this scheme adopt sustainable fishing methods. 

Eligibility for the scheme is primarily focused on registered cooperative societies in the fisheries sector. 

These societies must demonstrate a history of operation but have become inactive due to various challenges. 

The age limit for individual fishermen is not explicitly defined, but they must be at least 18 years old to be part of the cooperative. 

Income criteria for eligibility are set at a maximum annual income of ₹2 lakh for fishermen. 

The application process for the reactivation of societies involves several steps. 

First, the cooperative society must submit a proposal to the Department of Fisheries in West Bengal. 

This proposal should include details of past operations and reasons for inactivity. 

The society must also outline a plan for reactivation and how the funds will be utilized. 

Required documents include the society's registration certificate, a list of members, and a detailed project report. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it will be reviewed by the Department of Fisheries. 

The review process typically takes about 30 days. 

If approved, the society will receive the funds in a single installment. 

Disbursement of funds is expected to occur within 15 days of approval. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Fisheries, Government of West Bengal. 

The department has designated specific officials to oversee the implementation and monitoring of the scheme. 

Fisheries cooperative societies are encouraged to engage with local fisheries officers for guidance. 

The government has also set up a helpline for queries related to the application process. 

The helpline number is available on the official website of the Department of Fisheries. 

The Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana aims to address the challenges faced by fishermen due to the COVID-19 pandemic. 

The pandemic severely impacted the livelihoods of many fishermen, leading to a decline in fish production and sales. 

By reactivating cooperative societies, the government aims to create a support system for fishermen. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of collective bargaining power for fishermen. 

Through cooperative societies, fishermen can negotiate better prices for their catch. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹100 crore for the entire Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana. 

This budget includes funds for the reactivation of cooperative societies as well as other welfare measures. 

The scheme is expected to create job opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

It will also contribute to the overall economic development of coastal communities in West Bengal. 

The government plans to monitor the progress of the reactivated societies through regular audits. 

These audits will help ensure that funds are utilized effectively and that societies are functioning as intended. 

The Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana is part of a broader initiative to promote sustainable fisheries in India. 

The government is also promoting the use of technology in fishing practices. 

Fishermen will be encouraged to adopt digital platforms for selling their catch. 

This will help in reducing middlemen and increasing their profit margins. 

The scheme aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The reactivation of fisheries cooperative societies is a step towards achieving this goal. 

The government is also collaborating with various NGOs to provide additional support to fishermen. 

These collaborations aim to enhance the capacity of cooperative societies through training and resource sharing. 

The Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana is a comprehensive approach to uplift the fisheries sector in West Bengal. 

It addresses both immediate financial needs and long-term sustainability goals. 

The scheme is expected to have a multiplier effect on the local economy. 

By improving the livelihoods of fishermen, it will also benefit related sectors such as fish processing and marketing. 

The government is committed to ensuring transparency in the implementation of this scheme. 

Regular updates and reports will be published to keep stakeholders informed. 

This initiative is a significant move towards empowering fishermen and enhancing their socio-economic status. 

The reactivation of fisheries cooperative societies is crucial for building resilience in the fisheries sector. 

The Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana is a testament to the government's commitment to the welfare of fishermen in West Bengal. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to create a sustainable and prosperous future for the fishing community.
